source_text: In Proverbia (fragmenta) 75 ∆ιὰ τοῦ οἴνου καὶ τοῦ ἄρτου τὰ ἀντίτυπα τῶν σωματικῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ κηρύττει μελῶν. 76 Τὸν Χριστὸν λέγει Σοφίαν, τὴν αἰσθητὴν αὐτῆς εἰκόνα, διαγράφων τὴν ὁρατὴν φρόνησιν τήν τε ἐμπορίαν αὐτῆς <πρὸ> πάντων ἀσπαστέαν σημαίνων· καὶ οὐδὲν αὐτῇ κακίας εἶδος ἢ πανουργίας ἀντιτασσόμενον ἰσχύει· τοῖς γὰρ ἐρῶσιν αὐτῆς πρόδηλον γνώρισμα παριστῶν, ἐκβοᾷ μετ' εὐφημίας· εὔγνωστός ἐστι πᾶσι, καὶ πᾶν δὲ τίμιον οὐκ ἄξιον αὐτῆς.
thought_title: Wisdom as Christ through wine bread prudence and merchandise
orientation: Eustathius opens his commentary on Proverbs by identifying the wine and bread as representations of Christ's bodily members, and by naming Christ as Wisdom whose visible image is prudence and whose merchandise is to be embraced above all.
pass_a_gloss: Through the wine and the bread it proclaims the representations of the bodily members of Christ. It says Christ is Wisdom, depicting her perceptible image, the visible prudence, and signifying her merchandise as to be embraced before all things; and no form of wickedness or craftiness opposing her prevails; for presenting a clear sign of recognition to those who love her, she cries out with good report; she is well-known to all, and every precious thing is not worthy of her.

choices.why: Locked glossary sense for the bread and wine as corresponding types of Christ's bodily members; banned terms antitypes corresponding types avoided.
Locked glossary term for the personified Wisdom of Proverbs identified with Christ; banned Sophia avoided.
Locked glossary sense for visible prudence as Wisdom's image; banned practical wisdom avoided.
Locked glossary sense for Wisdom's merchandise to be embraced above all; banned gain traffic avoided.
εὐφημία means praise or good report, not clarity; the previous word πρόδηλον already conveys clear.
πρόδηλον means clear or evident; γνῶρισμα means sign or token of recognition; together they give a clear sign of recognition.

pass_b_english: Through wine and bread Proverbs proclaims the representations of Christ's bodily members.
It calls Christ Wisdom, depicting her visible image as visible prudence and indicating that her merchandise is to be embraced above all things.
No form of wickedness or craftiness that opposes her has any power.
For it cries out with good report, presenting to those who love her a clear sign of recognition: she is well-known to all, and every precious thing is not worthy of her.
notes: The source text includes a critical sign <πρὸ> before πάντων indicating a probable reading πρὸ πάντων (before all things) which is adopted in the gloss.

problems.quote: For she cries out with good report to those who love her, presenting a clear sign of recognition
problems.source_quote: τοῖς γὰρ ἐρῶσιν αὐτῆς πρόδηλον γνώρισμα παριστῶν, ἐκβοᾷ μετ' εὐφημίας
problems.why: παριστῶν is masculine, same subject as λέγει: Proverbs presents the sign and cries out about Wisdom, not Wisdom herself.
problems.fix: For it cries out with good report, presenting to those who love her a clear sign of recognition: she is well-known to all, and every precious thing is not worthy of her.
problems.ruling: The participles διαγράφων, σημαίνων and παριστῶν are masculine and share the subject of λέγει, so Proverbs is the one who ἐκβοᾷ. 'She cries out' wrongly makes Wisdom the speaker.

fixed: Fixed agency error: παριστῶν is masculine nominative singular referring to Proverbs (same subject as λέγει), not Wisdom. Changed 'she' to 'it', restructured to show Proverbs presents the sign to lovers and cries out about Wisdom's words.
